title: Finite normal residue models for weakly etale Nagata algebras
statement: Let A and B be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], f:A->B weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], and A Nagata [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. For any prime q of B and finite extension L/kappa(q), there is a B-subalgebra D of L, finite over B and an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], with fraction field L. Moreover there is a domain R finite over A and an injective weakly etale map R->D. R can be chosen in the universe of A; no finiteness of kappa(q)/kappa(f^-1(q)) is assumed.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings; Stacks Project, Algebra and More on Algebra
source.place: Greco Theorem 5.3(ii), pp. 146–147, normalization construction in the existing parent node steps 3–7; Stacks Tags 092Q, 0C22, 030C for field fibres, normality ascent and normal factors. The finite-generator and fraction-field glue is written out in this node.

proof.text: For p=f^-1(q), base change to kappa(p). The fibre is absolutely flat. Localize the fibre at the kernel of its map to kappa(q): the localization is a weakly etale field extension, hence algebraic. Images of B are integral over kappa(p); their fractions give algebraicity of kappa(q). Adjoin a finite kappa(q)-spanning set of L over kappa(p), obtaining a finite subextension L0 with kappa(q)L0=L. Shrink L0 to Type u using Module.Finite.small and Shrink.algEquiv.

Normalize A/p in the small finite field L0. The Nagata hypothesis makes this integral closure R finite over A/p, hence over A. The finite-extension normalization lemmas make R an integrally closed domain with fraction field L0; it is Noetherian by module finiteness.

Set C=R tensor_A B. Base change makes R->C weakly etale; finite tensor base change makes C finite over B and Noetherian. Every fibre is absolutely flat, so its prime localizations are fields and are normal. Normality of prime localizations of R and flat normal-fibre ascent give normality of C.

Map C to L by multiplication, with image D and kernel Q. The restriction to R is injective, so Q contracts to zero. Any prime below Q also contracts to zero. The fibre order isomorphism over the zero prime sends both to comparable primes in an absolutely flat ring, whose primes are maximal. Hence they agree, and Q is minimal.

The normal Noetherian ring C is reduced and has finitely many minimal primes. The normal decomposition theorem writes it as a finite product of normal domains. A product prime selects a factor; minimality of Q identifies Q with that projection kernel. Thus D is isomorphic to a normal domain factor. The projection is localization at its coordinate idempotent, by IsLocalization.away_of_isIdempotentElem_of_mul. Composition makes R->D weakly etale and its restriction remains injective.

The image D is finite over B as the surjective image of the finite B-module C. Embed its fraction field in L and call the image F. It contains images of B and fractions thereof, hence kappa(q); it contains R and its fractions, hence L0. The finite kappa(q)-spanning set chosen for L lies in L0, so F=L. Represent each element by a fraction in D, with nonzero denominator.

from.place: Normalization models for weakly etale Nagata and J-2 ascent, parent node proof steps 3–7.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_residue_model_of_weaklyEtale
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.WeaklyEtale) (hNagata : IsNagataRing A)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime] (L : Type v) [Field L]
    [Algebra q.ResidueField L] [Algebra B L] [IsScalarTower B q.ResidueField L]
    [Module.Finite q.ResidueField L] :
    ∃ D : Subalgebra B L, Module.Finite B D ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed D ∧
      (∀ x : L, ∃ b c : D, (c : L) ≠ 0 ∧ x = (b : L) / (c : L)) ∧
      ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R) (_ : Algebra A R),
        Module.Finite A R ∧ ∃ (_ : Algebra R D),
          Algebra.WeaklyEtale R D ∧ Function.Injective (algebraMap R D)
